text: Lesson one was one conversation about one request. This lesson turns that conversation into a habit you can run on any vague ask for the rest of your career, not just this project.

Five questions, every time: what's the metric, and is it actually defined? What's it compared against? What's the scope, population, time window, segment? Who's the audience, and what decision will they make? And what's the cadence, one-time, or does this need to refresh on a schedule?
Watch for three red flags: I'll just guess the time window, they didn't say who else sees it so I'll assume just them, and it's probably one-time. Each one is a guess wearing a disguise.
Close every intake the same way, with a two-minute email restating exactly how you read the request, before you touch a single tool. Cheap insurance if the answer is yes.
Same five questions, any request. Next: stress-testing the churn definition itself against real, messy data.
